Did a test run with golden beets from the grocery store since I've never canned before

Both of them sealed properly, yes they're pickled not just canned. I know you can't regular boil can low acid foods without pickling as well. I'm not sure how long I should leave these minimum before taking some out to try. A few weeks? A month? A few months?

How do those taste? I usually ferment my beets but can only get the bulls heart variety here.

5% salt brine, 4 cardamon pods, 1 TSP mustard seed. 2 pounds beets.

I actually haven't ever had a golden beet but supposedly they're a little less brutal on the beet taste that a lot of people find offputting. I'll make an update with how they taste in a couple weeks. I used a few different recipes to get a better, more complete picture of the canning process. I used just the pickling solution from one recipe, the canning process from a different recipe, and used a few bits and pieces from yet more recipes to try to be as safe as possible. Some people were recommending really short boiling times or stupid "sterilization" techniques that I didn't feel safe about so I ignored those parts of those recipes.

The brine was just a random amount of salt I felt was appropriate, somewhere around a half tablespoon. I like my shit salty anyway. Mostly vinegar. Some of the beet juice from the initial boiling (I dumped it out accidentally and had to use water but would have used the beet juice to reduce flavor loss). A bunch of sugar. And on top of the beets in the jars I threw some premade pickling spice mix.

So I tried some beets a few days ago while I was high and the sweetness/spiciness (from the pickling spice) was a little overwhelming so I put them in the fridge and ate the rest today. They're really good, flavor has gone pretty well all the way through already. Very mild on the beet flavor but it's a really lovely-textured medium for carrying the acidity, sweetness, saltiness, and spices over.

Can I get a quick rundown on your method? Also, did you buy a canner?

lol fuck no I didn't buy shit except the jars

Cook your food, let it cool off in the corner while you continue and then peel it once it's fairly well cooled off.

Make the pickling solution (basically ALL foods NEED to be pickled in a solution that's mostly vinegar or you will get botulism even from sealed and "sterilized" jars). While that's coming to a boil, sterilize jars/rings/lids by boiling them in water for 10 minutes. Take the jars and pieces out and let them cool off and AIR dry, nothing should touch the surfaces that will be inside the jar after this point except boiling substances.

The jars don't have to cool completely, and probably shouldn't actually, so put in your shit you're canning, throw in some pickling spices if you want, and pour the boiling pickling solution over the food in the jar, leaving at least a half an inch of air space (no food or brine) at the top of the jar. Good idea to take a piece of paper towel and dip it in the boiling water, and wipe off the very top rim of the jar for a good seal.

Put on the lids quickly, and LIGHTLY screw on your rings, if you tighten them all the way it's going to fuck up the lid because the pressure from the last boiling step will bend the lid. They just barely need to make contact with the lids.

Jars back into ALREADY-boiling (don't throw hot jars in cold water and bring it up to temp) water, for 10 minutes at least (nothing wrong with slightly longer).

Take jars out, tilt slightly to get the water off the lids, and then just let them sit there and they should all seal. If any of them don't seal it's straight to the fridge and they must be eaten within about a week I believe. Though I'd personally probably go up to 2 weeks.

If you want to can fruit and vegetables without pickling, you need to buy a pressure canner or again, you'll get botulism because boiling water at atmospheric pressure isn't hot enough. High pressure + high temperature, or high acidity + 212f = safe
Also take the rings off the jars once they cool off, they're not necessary at that point and they'll last longer.
